description: Deviations from the literal text of SPEC.md, with justification. A deviation is permitted ONLY when the literal text is unsatisfiable or strictly weaker than what it intends, and only when the intended content is proved in full. Every entry names the SPEC clause, what was changed, why, and the declaration that carries the intended strength. Silent deviation is forbidden.

deviations.specText: theorem costed_erase_iff_plain_run : Wasm.CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation <-> Wasm.Run module invocation (eraseCosts costedTrace) observation
deviations.issue: The literal biconditional is FALSE, and this is now PROVED rather than argued. `costedTrace` is universally quantified, and the right-hand side mentions it only through `eraseCosts costedTrace`, which is not injective: it discards the installed byte count of `enterGemm`, the requested page count of `memoryGrowSucceed`, and it identifies the whole ordinary-rule family in `Event.step`. A trace carrying forged cost labels whose erasure equals a valid plain trace therefore satisfies the right-hand side without being a costed run the machine can produce. The backward direction cannot hold for an arbitrary labelling.
refutedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.not_costed_erase_iff_plain_run -- for EVERY profile, not (forall module invocation costedTrace observation, CostedRun <-> Run (eraseCosts costedTrace))
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimalModule -- a module that passes `Wasm.validate` (minimalModule_validate), together with a three-step maximal run of it (minimal_finiteExecution)
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.forgedTrace -- [enterGemm 1, i32Const, returnGemm 0]; the run installs ZERO raw bytes, so the machine's label is `enterGemm 0`
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimal_run -- the right-hand side HOLDS of the forged trace
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimal_not_costedRun -- the left-hand side FAILS, under any profile
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.erase_enterGemm_eq -- erasure discards the payload the two sides disagree about
deviations.resolution: `Wasm.costed_erase_iff_plain_run` adds the minimal side condition `CostedLabelling module invocation costedTrace` to the right-hand side, and the intended content is proved separately and unconditionally.
intendedContentProvedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.costed_run_iff_plain_run  -- (exists costedTrace, CostedRun ...) <-> Run module invocation observation.trace observation; NO side condition
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.costedRun_of_run          -- erasure completeness: every plain run has a costed labelling erasing back to it
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.costedRun_erase           -- erasure soundness
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.costed_erase_forward      -- the forward direction of SPEC's display, unconditionally
deviations.strengthEffect: STRENGTHENING. The forward direction is strictly stronger than SPEC's (CostedRun -> Run AND the labelling is machine-produced). The existentially quantified form carries SPEC's full intent with no side condition, so nothing SPEC asserts is lost.
deviations.amendmentText: SPEC 7.5 should state the erasure theorem in the existentially quantified form `(exists costedTrace, CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation) <-> Run module invocation observation.trace observation`, which is true as written.

deviations.specText: A plan loop iterates a number of times determined by its extent.
deviations.issue: An UNCLAMPED register-bounded loop would make the pre-existing theorem Plan.steps_le_stepBound FALSE: that theorem bounds executed steps by a static Nat computed from the plan text, and no fixed number bounds a loop whose trip count is an arbitrary register value (take body = setReg and an arbitrarily large extent register).
deviations.resolution: Plan.loopReg runs Nat.min (m.reg extentReg) loopRegMaxTrips times, with loopRegMaxTrips = 4294967295.
intendedContentProvedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_trips_from_memory -- trip count IS the memory word, given n <= loopRegMaxTrips
WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_eq_loopNest -- agrees with the literal-extent form
WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_zero -- no clamp hypothesis needed
deviations.strengthEffect: NEUTRAL IN REACH. loopRegMaxTrips is the released i32 ceiling and equals maxRawExtent, so the clamp is unreachable for any configuration the released ABI can present or any value the compiled i32 locals can hold. It preserves an existing theorem instead of weakening it.
deviations.amendmentText: SPEC 11.1 should state that a register-bounded loop's trip count is clamped at the profile's address-space ceiling, so that a static step bound remains derivable from plan text.

deviations.specText: theorem incremental_eq_full_rebuild (hupdate : (Atlas.accumulate budget state delta).result = .complete successor) : Atlas.canonicalize successor.body = Atlas.canonicalize (Atlas.semanticRebuildBody (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations))
deviations.issue: The literal statement is FALSE, and this is PROVED, not argued. `state` is universally quantified over `Atlas.UnsealedState`, a type that carries neither a scope restriction nor a coherence obligation. (a) SCOPE: `Atlas.semanticRebuildBody` takes only the declaration base, which names no objective, profile or problem identity, so it always answers `Scope.unscoped`; `Atlas.semanticApplyBody` preserves the scope of the state it updates; `Atlas.canonicalize` copies the three identities verbatim. Any state whose objective identity is not `nullId` therefore falsifies the equation for EVERY budget and delta. (b) COHERENCE: a state may record a semantic half its declaration base does not derive, and the surplus survives canonicalisation.
refutedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.not_incremental_eq_full_rebuild -- not (forall budget state delta successor, accumulate ... = complete successor -> canonicalize successor.body = canonicalize (semanticRebuildBody ...))
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.incremental_ne_full_rebuild_of_objectiveId -- the scope failure is systematic: it holds for every budget, delta and successor whenever state.body.objectiveId is not nullId
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.Counterexample.scopedState -- a COHERENT state (scopedState_coherent) in a scope of its own, on which the equation fails
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.not_incremental_eq_full_rebuild_unscoped -- restricting SPEC's statement to unscoped states does NOT save it: the coherence hypothesis is doing work of its own
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.Counterexample.incoherent_ne_full_rebuild -- the witness for the line above: an UNSCOPED state that records one stray semantic object its empty declaration base does not derive
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.Counterexample.scopedState_accumulate -- the update instance used is `Delta.empty`, whose completion is itself required by SPEC 12.5's `update_empty_fixed_point`
deviations.resolution: `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` states SPEC's equation under exactly the two hypotheses the refutations show to be load-bearing: `Atlas.Coherent state.body` and `state.body.scope = Atlas.Scope.unscoped`. The general form, which fixes the scope objection by rebuilding in the state's OWN scope instead of assuming it away, is proved without the scope hypothesis and is the one the repository uses.
intendedContentProvedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild_scoped -- canonicalize successor.body = canonicalize (semanticRebuildBodyWith state.body.scope (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations)); NO scope hypothesis
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild_exact -- the same equation BEFORE canonicalisation, which is strictly stronger
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild -- SPEC's literal equation under the two necessary hypotheses
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.semanticApplyBody_coherent -- coherence is preserved by every update, so the hypothesis is discharged rather than assumed at every state the pipeline produces
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.rebuild_coherent -- and by the rebuild that starts a lifecycle
deviations.strengthEffect: NEUTRAL IN REACH, DISCLOSED AS WEAKER. The two hypotheses cannot be dropped: `not_incremental_eq_full_rebuild` proves no theorem of SPEC's literal shape exists. `incremental_eq_full_rebuild_scoped` carries SPEC's intent -- incremental update equals full rebuild from the same declaration base -- with the scope hypothesis removed rather than assumed, and `incremental_eq_full_rebuild_exact` strengthens it past canonicalisation. A state produced by `Atlas.rebuild` is coherent (`rebuild_coherent`) and `Atlas.accumulate` preserves coherence (`semanticApplyBody_coherent`), so the coherence hypothesis excludes only hand-built states such as the counterexample's. The binding in Conformance/RequiredSignatures.lean remains AMENDED and the SPEC 15 name remains OUTSTANDING: nothing here is counted as discharged.
deviations.amendmentText: SPEC 12.5 should state rebuild equivalence in the state's own scope -- `Atlas.canonicalize successor.body = Atlas.canonicalize (Atlas.semanticRebuildBodyWith state.body.scope (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations))` -- over a state whose body is coherent, since `semanticRebuildBody` provably cannot reproduce a scope its only input does not name.

deviations.specText: theorem attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative (hsealed : Atlas.SealCertificate state core) (hprofile : Wasm.ProfileId profile = core.profileId) (hproblem : Gemm.ProblemId problem = core.problemId) (hobjective : Cost.ObjectiveId objective = core.objectiveId) (hc : Universal.ProfileValid profile candidateBytes) (heval : Universal.SystemEvaluationRel profile problem candidateBytes evaluation) (hscore : objective.score evaluation.cost <= core.baselineScore) : Atlas.AttentionContains core candidateBytes \/ Atlas.HasSoundExclusionCertificate core candidateBytes evaluation
deviations.issue: The statement is FALSE, and this is PROVED, not argued. `state` and `core` are universally quantified over `Atlas.UnsealedState` and `Atlas.SealCore`, and `Atlas.SealCertificate` is the conjunction of the seven deterministic checkers of Atlas/Certificate.lean. Not one of those checkers mentions a byte string, a decoder, a semantics or a cost: `attentionCompleteCheck` asks only that every object the state RECORDS is routed by some indexed signature, and it is satisfied -- with every root empty -- by a state that recorded nothing at all. The conclusion, by contrast, is about an arbitrary `candidateBytes` whose evaluated score is within the core's baseline. Nothing links the two, so a seal that declared nothing faces a real candidate it neither attends nor holds a retained certificate about. The gap is exactly SPEC 10.5's universal coverage obligation, and SPEC 12.2 gives the seal no way to discharge it. This is the attention counterpart of the fact `Atlas/CoverageScope.lean` already records for the cover check (`universalCoverCompleteCheck_scope_blind`), now with a counterexample instead of a blindness lemma.
refutedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative_is_false -- not (SPEC's statement), PARAMETRICALLY in the two predicates SPEC names but never defines: it holds for every `Contains` such that an attention root listing no signature contains no candidate, and every `Excluded` such that a certificate root listing no certificate identity supplies no RETAINED exclusion certificate (SPEC 12.2: 'legal only when a retained proof shows'). No choice of `Atlas.AttentionContains` / `Atlas.HasSoundExclusionCertificate` meeting those two conditions makes the statement true.

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.honesty_conditions_satisfiable -- the two conditions are satisfiable: this file's own `AttentionContains` and `HasSoundExclusionCertificate` meet them, so the refutation is not a conditional with an unsatisfiable antecedent

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.undeclared_witness_is_missed -- the witness: at the constructed release scope, `Release.witnessBytes` is optimum-relevant to a sealed core (profile valid, evaluated, scoring exactly at the baseline) whose attention root lists NO signature and whose certificate root lists NO certificate

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.sealCertificateAt -- the counterexample's seal is not weakened: all seven deterministic checkers are discharged by the proved checker results of Atlas/Rebuild.lean, at an arbitrary `baselineScore` (no checker reads it)

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.no_listed_exclusion_ground_for_witness -- and no exclusion certificate could have been sound anyway: of SPEC's three listed grounds, `empty` is contradicted by `Release.witness_profileValid`, `cannotBeatBound` by the candidate TYING the baseline, and `reconstructibleElsewhere` by the core attending nothing

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative_is_false_for_listed_grounds -- the same refutation with the retention requirement dropped entirely, under the reading that SPEC's three listed grounds are the legal ones

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative_is_false_at_every_evaluator -- and it does not depend on the evaluator the counterexample names: it fails at EVERY `Universal.Decider` that evaluates the witness bytes at all, by `Universal.systemEvaluation_subsingleton`
deviations.resolution: `Atlas.attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative` is NOT DECLARED in this repository, under any hypotheses. SPEC 15's name stays outstanding, no declaration wears it, and Conformance/RequiredSignatures.lean carries no binding for it -- an AMENDED binding must be closed by `:= @<the SPEC name>`, and declaring a weaker theorem under that name is exactly what this deviation refuses to do. The intended content is proved under a different name, `Atlas.attention_no_declared_optimum_relevant_false_negative`, which carries every one of SPEC's hypotheses plus exactly two: `Atlas.Coherent state.body`, the standing well-formedness condition of Atlas/Update.lean (established by every rebuild, preserved by every update, and the same hypothesis DEV-004 found load bearing); and membership of the candidate in `state.body.declarationBase.declarations`, which the refutation proves load bearing. Its conclusion is STRONGER than SPEC's: the left disjunct is proved outright, in both the core-level reading (`Atlas.AttentionContains`) and the strictly stronger `attend`-level reading (`Atlas.AttentionRoutes`), so no exclusion certificate is needed and none is offered.
intendedContentProvedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.attention_no_declared_optimum_relevant_false_negative -- a DECLARED optimum-relevant candidate on a coherent state is routed by `attend` and contained in the sealed core; it also returns the `Atlas.OptimumRelevant` witness, so no hypothesis is idle

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.declared_witness_is_routed -- NON-VACUITY: the same real candidate as the counterexample, declared this time, is actually returned by the index. `Atlas.OptimumRelevant` is inhabited, so the theorem is not about an empty class

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.attentionRoutes_of_indexesCandidate -- the routing mechanism drops nothing it indexes: from an index entry to `attend`'s answer, through the filter, the flatMap and the duplicate removal
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.attentionContains_of_attentionRoutes -- and the seal records the signature of everything `attend` returns, extracted from `attentionCompleteCheck` rather than assumed

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.OptimumRelevant -- relevance is defined from the objective, the candidate bytes and the decider ALONE. It mentions no attention index, no `attend`, no signature and no seal check, so the theorem is not `rfl` and relevance is not defined through the index
deviations.strengthEffect: NEUTRAL IN REACH, DISCLOSED AS WEAKER, AND NOT COUNTED. The two hypotheses cannot be dropped: `attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative_is_false` proves no theorem of SPEC's literal shape exists for any honest reading of the two undefined predicates. The added hypothesis is not an assumption that the index already holds the candidate -- it says only that the candidate reached the Atlas as a DECLARATION, and the indexing is then derived (`Atlas.attentionEntryOf`) and the routing PROVED. What remains open is that every profile-valid byte string is declared, which is SPEC 10.5's universal coverage obligation and is untouched here. No SPEC 15 name is declared, no signature binding is added, and `xtask claims required` continues to report `Atlas.attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative` MISSING -- the ledger is unchanged at 37 discharged of 58.
deviations.amendmentText: SPEC 12.2 should state attention completeness relative to what the Atlas was given -- over a state whose body is `Atlas.Coherent` and a candidate in its declaration base -- and should state the byte-universe half separately, as SPEC 10.5 already does, instead of asking a seal built from seven checkers that never read a byte to carry a proposition quantified over all byte strings. SPEC should also define `Atlas.AttentionContains` and `Atlas.HasSoundExclusionCertificate`, which section 12.2 uses without defining; leaving them open is what makes a vacuous discharge available to a less careful implementation.

deviations.specText: theorem validate_bool_iff (module : Wasm.Module) : Wasm.validate module = true <-> Wasm.DeclarativelyValid module
deviations.issue: THE DEFECT IS IN THE PINNED SPECIFICATION, NOT IN SPEC.md AND NOT IN THIS TRANSCRIPTION. This is the first deviation filed against the VENDORED Core 3.0 source rather than against SPEC.md's own text. The left-to-right direction of SPEC 7.3's biconditional is FALSE against the declarative side as pinned, and this is PROVED, not argued. `Instrs_ok/seq` of `vendor/wasm-spec/specification/wasm-3.0/2.3-validation.instructions.spectec` types the HEAD instruction with the principal relation `Instr_ok` and requires the TAIL's domain to be EXACTLY the head's codomain. The only rules that can adjust a type are `Instrs_ok/sub`, which preserves domain length because `Resulttype_sub` is a synchronised iteration over both sequences, and `Instrs_ok/frame`, which only makes a domain LONGER; both apply to SEQUENCES, and there is no `Instr_ok/sub` and no `Instr_ok/frame` anywhere in the vendored tree. A head that produces fewer operands than the tail consumes therefore can never be composed. `(I32.CONST c) (BINOP I32 ADD)` is the smallest instance: the pinned rules give it NO instruction type in ANY context, so no function body performing binary arithmetic is `Expr_ok`, no module containing one is `Module_ok`, and `DeclarativelyValid` as pinned is close to vacuous while `Wasm.validate` (which implements the appendix algorithm) accepts such modules. THE PINNED SOURCE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS POINT: `vendor/wasm-spec/document/core/valid/instructions.rst:1357-1366`, at the SAME commit, says the derivation exists and attributes the weakening of `eps -> I32` to `I32 -> I32 I32` to subsumption; that is not an `Instrtype_sub` supertype (the lengths differ), it is `Instrs_ok/frame` applied to the singleton SEQUENCE, a step `seq` cannot consume because its head premise is `Instr_ok`. Rendered prose cannot distinguish `Instr_ok` from `Instrs_ok` -- both print as `C |- ... : it` -- which is why the gap is invisible in the published document and bites only a mechanisation. UPSTREAM AGREES, AFTER THE PIN: WebAssembly/spec issue #2194 ('instrs_ok/seq's principality requirement is slightly over-restrictive', raoxiaojia, 2026-06-22) reports it in the same terms, and PR #2197 ('[spec] Fix instr sequence typing rules to actually be composable') merged the repair as commit bd4633aced30b720ff62b44cf00c03ece792f008 on 2026-06-23 -- nine months after the pinned commit 9d36019973201a19f9c9ebb0f10828b2fe2374aa (2025-09-26). The vendored file is byte-identical to upstream blob bfd71e57ff457c61f546e0a308b99740fda02158 at the pin, so the transcription is not at fault; and the argument is about LENGTHS alone, so no operand-order or list-orientation convention in this repository could create or remove it.
refutedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Validate.Instrs_ok.cons_inv -- THE DEFECT IN FULL GENERALITY: for EVERY context, head instruction, tail and instruction type, a pinned derivation of `i :: is` contains an `Instr_ok` typing of `i` whose codomain is EXACTLY the domain of a pinned typing of `is`; `sub` and `frame` do not change a derivation's subject, so they cannot intervene between head and tail

WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Validate.Instrs_ok.cons_untypable_of_arity -- the general REJECTION SCHEMA: if the head can never produce n operands and the tail always consumes at least n, the pinned rules give the composition no type, in every context, at every instruction type
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Validate.Instrs_ok.binop_dom_length -- every pinned type of the singleton `(BINOP nt op)` has domain length at least 2
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Validate.Instrs_ok.const_binop_untypable -- forall C nt c op is it, Instrs_ok C is it -> is = [CONST nt c, BINOP nt op] -> False; the n = 2 instance of the schema
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Validate.Instrs_ok.const_const_binop_untypable -- the same one instruction further out
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Validate.Expr_ok.const_const_binop_untypable -- and hence NO context gives that expression a result type, which is what makes the pinned `Module_ok` near-vacuous

WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.gapModule_not_ok -- THE VACUITY AT MODULE LEVEL: forall mt, not (Module_ok gapModule mt), where gapModule is `(func (result i32) i32.const 0 i32.const 0 i32.add)` and `Wasm.Core.Validate.validate gapModule = true` is checked by evaluation beside it. This is the exact obstruction to SPEC 7.3's biconditional
deviations.resolution: The pin is NOT advanced: advancing past bd4633a would change the vendored blob set and the Core 3.0 rule inventory (it adds an `Instrs_ok/instr` rule and carries unrelated deltas). Instead the repository states the amended judgment explicitly, in `WasmGemmGnaf/Wasm/Core/Validation/InstructionsAmended.lean`, and carries this entry as its written justification. THE AMENDMENT IS ONE MODIFIED PREMISE AND NO NEW RULE: `Instrs_ok'/seq` carries the frame `t_0*` INSIDE the composition -- `C |- instr_1 instr_2* : (t_0* t_1*) ->_(x_1* x_2*) t_3*` from `Instr_ok: C |- instr_1 : t_1* ->_(x_1*) t_2*`, `Resulttype_ok: C |- t_0* : OK` and `Instrs_ok: ... |- instr_2* : (t_0* t_2*) ->_(x_2*) t_3*`. `empty`, `sub` and `frame` are unchanged, and `t_0* = eps` is exactly the pinned rule. This is the frame the classic prose rule for instruction sequences already carries ('there is a sequence of value types t_0* such that t_2* = t_0* t*') and the second of the two repairs issue #2194 proposes; upstream took the first (lift the head to `Instrs_ok`, adding a rule and making `seq`'s subject an append that no longer determines the split). Because `Instr_ok/block`, `Instr_ok/loop` and `Instr_ok/if` type their bodies with the sequence judgment, the amendment is propagated through them by a mutual `Instr_ok'` that LIFTS every pinned instruction rule unchanged and re-states only those three; otherwise the vacuity would survive one nesting level down. NO COVERAGE MARKER is attached to any declaration in the amended file, so the Core 3.0 inventory stays at 1288 of 1288 with validation rules 256 of 256. `Wasm.validate_iff_declarative` remains OUTSTANDING and is NOT counted as discharged; when it is attempted it SHALL be stated over `Instrs_ok'` with this entry cited, never over the pinned relation.

WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Expr_ok.to_amended -- the same at expression level
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.const_binop -- THE DERIVATION THE PINNED RULES CANNOT EXPRESS: C |- (I32.CONST c) (BINOP I32 ADD) : I32 -> I32, in EVERY context
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.const_const_binop -- (CONST) (CONST) (BINOP) : eps -> I32
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Expr_ok'.const_const_binop -- the same sequence as an EXPRESSION, directly refuting the pinned Expr_ok.const_const_binop_untypable under the amendment

WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.binop_dom_length -- NON-WIDENING, the check that matters: under the AMENDED rules every type of the singleton (BINOP nt op) STILL has domain length at least 2. This is the very lemma that drives the negative result, re-proved for the amendment: composability was bought by supplying operands from the frame, NOT by letting a domain shrink
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.nil_length -- the empty sequence is still balanced under the amendment, in every context at every type
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.const_length -- (CONST nt c) still pushes EXACTLY one operand
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.binop_length -- (BINOP nt op) still nets exactly one operand off the stack
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.not_const_nil -- a pushed constant still cannot vanish: no amended type eps -> eps
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.not_binop_unary -- BINOP still cannot be fed one operand
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Instrs_ok'.not_binop_balanced -- BINOP still cannot leave both operands behind

WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Func_ok.to_amended -- NO REGRESSION at function level: every pinned Func_ok is a Func_ok'; the amended rule replaces the ONE Expr_ok premise and leaves the type lookup, Expand and Local_ok premises verbatim

WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Core.Func_ok'.gapFunc -- THE VACUITY CLOSED AT THE LEVEL IT WAS STATED: the body of gapModule, which gapModule_not_ok proves the pinned rules cannot type, IS Func_ok' at exactly the deftype the module's type section declares
deviations.strengthEffect: STRICTLY WIDER THAN THE PINNED RELATION, BY EXACTLY THE INTENDED AMOUNT, AND DISCLOSED. `Instrs_ok'` properly contains `Instrs_ok` (`Instrs_ok.to_amended`), and it must: the pinned relation cannot type ordinary WebAssembly, so any repository theorem quantified over pinned-valid modules would be the most dangerous kind of vacuity. The widening is bounded in the direction that matters. The four arity theorems hold for the AMENDED relation in every context at every instruction type: the empty sequence stays balanced, CONST still pushes exactly one operand, BINOP still consumes at least two and nets exactly minus one. `Instrs_ok'.binop_dom_length` is literally the pinned `Instrs_ok.binop_dom_length` re-proved against the amended rules, so the amendment provably did not achieve composability by weakening arity discipline -- the failure mode an over-wide fix would exhibit. No soundness or `validate_iff_declarative` theorem is claimed here; SPEC 15's `Wasm.validate_iff_declarative` stays OUTSTANDING and CIRCULAR as before, and nothing in this entry is counted as discharged.
deviations.amendmentText: SPEC.md needs no amendment: SPEC 7.3's `validate_bool_iff` is the right proposition, and it becomes true once the declarative side is the amended relation. The amendment belongs UPSTREAM, and upstream has already made it: WebAssembly/spec PR #2197 (bd4633aced30b720ff62b44cf00c03ece792f008). The repository action item is a pin decision, not a SPEC edit -- advance `authority/manifest.json`'s `wasmCore.commit` past bd4633a and re-derive the rule inventory, or keep the pin and carry this entry. The pin is currently kept.

amendments.was: SPEC 5 specified Lean tooling under Tools/ (Main.lean, EmitArtifact.lean, GenerateManifest.lean, GenerateConformance.lean, CheckClaims.lean, CheckAxioms.lean, CheckSources.lean, Reproduce.lean) and stated: 'The Rust workspace ... SHALL be removed after the Lean conformance replacement passes. No Rust code is part of the final product or proof path.'
amendments.now: SPEC 5.1 'Language boundary' fixes two languages. Lean 4 is the proof and implementation language: every definition, theorem, semantics, cost model, plan, compiler and artifact-producing term lives under WasmGemmGnaf/ and is checked by the Lean kernel. Rust is the infrastructure and tooling language: the release gate, source and firewall scans, claim and axiom audits, manifest and documentation generators, mutation suite and reproduction driver live under xtask/ and are driven by the Justfile.
amendments.rationale: Requested by the repository owner. The boundary preserves the property the original clause protected: the trust base stays the Lean kernel. xtask CHECKS whether the kernel has discharged an obligation; it never DECIDES one. A tool that decided a proof obligation would move the trust base outside the kernel, which SPEC 4 forbids.
constraintsAdded: The boundary is one-directional: nothing under WasmGemmGnaf/ may depend on xtask.
No Rust code is on the proof path.
xtask SHALL build with the Rust standard library alone -- a network-fetched crate would be a network-fetched input to release verification, which SPEC 4 forbids.
Rust source SHALL NOT appear under WasmGemmGnaf/, and Lean source SHALL NOT appear under xtask/.
amendments.supersedes: DEV-003 (never filed; the deviation was amended into the SPEC instead)
